assign.outcome:
**Lighten and darken got names, and a page that proves what they do.** Six tokens, a live study, and the layout skill's new rule.

![](color-1280.jpg)

**1. The tokens.** You already had them under other names — `framework.css`'s `:root` carries `--shade-aNN` (black at an alpha) and `--paper-aNN` (white at an alpha), four rungs that double. So the six new names are **aliases**: `--lighten-1/2/3` and `--darken-1/2/3` are `--paper-a08/16/32` and `--shade-a08/16/32`. Nothing existing changed value and no new colour was mixed. One file touched: `public/framework/framework.css`, +34 lines, 0 removed.

**2. The study — [/imagine/design/color/](/imagine/design/color/).** Five grounds (white to black) x the six steps, every cell painted with the real token and labelled with the hex the browser actually composited and the contrast of your `--ink` on it, read live off the pixels. Then the accent: five saturations of one hue, each shown as a ground and as text on all five grounds, with **a hue slider and a saturation slider that repaint the whole page**. The sentence at the top is computed, not typed, and rewrites as you drag:

> At hue 18 degrees, your accent at 100% saturation carries body text on dark gray, black - and used as a ground it takes ink text. Draining the saturation out of it changes nothing: at this hue every rung lands on the same grounds. Drag the hue slider round to a blue or a violet and watch that stop being true.

That last clause is the finding: **saturation's effect on contrast depends on the hue.** At your orange, draining it moves nothing. At hue 240, 100% saturation passes on white at 4.5:1 and 25% fails at 2.6:1.

**3. The layout skill** gained one section, *Boxes, padding and contrast*, after *Rhythm*. It opens: *Does this thing need a box - a background different from its parent's? If yes, it needs padding: a fill with text jammed against its edge is not a box, it is a stain.* Then the ratio rule (4.5 for text, 3 for UI) with a link to the study, then your nine-point pre-build checklist - layout, navigation, structure, visual hierarchy, iceberg UX, color, focus, interaction, purpose and outcome - answered in a line each before the first factory call.

**Also:** the 2026-09-01 palette crawl that used to be this page is intact one click down at [palette/](/imagine/design/color/palette/), so level 1 is one screen. The record is in the page's own *decisions.md*, behind the disclosure at the bottom.

**Left, and why.** No lightness slider - lightness is pinned at your accent's own 69% so that only one thing changes between rungs; adding it would make the five rungs stop being comparable. The recorded numbers are light-mode - the page reads whatever `--ink` resolves to, so it is honest in dark too, but a side-by-side two-mode matrix would double the page, and the light/dark island trick already lives on the palette page. The usage snapshot was not refreshed - `ai/usage.json` is outside this task's fence.
